messages:
Alice Chen: Quick sync — Acme POC had burst failures during a load run. They saw intermittent 503s and a handful of degraded outputs. Ellen flagged this and wants to understand fallback behavior + any SLA impact. @Devon can you confirm what happened and proposed remediation?

Devon Park: On it. I pulled the last run logs. Looks like their request pattern caused queue pressure on the primary model pod group; our autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough so the router kicked the fallback policy. Fallback picked model-compact-v1 automatically.

Ellen Rivera: Confirm — the errors were around 11:23 UTC. We saw ~40 failed requests and ~120 that returned shorter, lower-quality responses (missing context). We need clear acceptance criteria for "acceptable fallback" so we can sign off.

Ravi Patel: For the POC acceptance we proposed: 95th pct latency < 250ms for interactive chat, and hallucination/regression rate <= 2% on the evaluation prompt set. If fallback leads to >2% regression we can't accept. Can we quantify expected regression for model-compact-v1 on their eval?

Devon Park: Good call. I'll run the eval suite against model-compact-v1 and model-standard-v2 and post numbers. My hunch: compact will have slightly higher token-level error but should stay <3% on most prompts; need to verify. Also propose we add an explicit header so client can detect fallback: X-Redwood-Fallback: model-compact-v1 (or blank).

Marisol Vega: Heads-up on BYO-KMS ask from Acme security questionnaire. If we do private or dedicated and they enable BYO-KMS, we need to confirm that key access is available to the inference host for wrapping/unwrapping. Fallback should not change key usage but we must document key-scoping and key-access audit events.

Jordan Li: Pasting the relevant excerpt from the runtime log for the incident:

```
[2026-04-12T11:23:14Z] router: recv req id=acme-req-9c1f
[2026-04-12T11:23:15Z] pod-scale: group=primary-models desired=6 current=4
[2026-04-12T11:23:15Z] router: enqueue depth=112 threshold=100 -> triggering fallback
[2026-04-12T11:23:15Z] router: fallback model=model-compact-v1, request_id=acme-req-9c1f
[2026-04-12T11:23:15Z] response: status=200 model=model-compact-v1 latency_ms=185 tokens=124
[2026-04-12T11:23:16Z] response: status=503 request_id=acme-req-9c4b
```

Devon Park: Thanks Jordan. That matches my read. Two immediate levers: 1) raise the enqueue threshold + faster autoscale; 2) add circuit-breaker + backpressure to return 429 when the tail latency will exceed SLOs instead of silently falling back. Option 2 is safer for correctness-sensitive workflows.

Ellen Rivera: If we add 429s we worry about user experience. Can the client opt into a "graceful fallback" mode (accept lower-quality but continue serving) vs "strict" mode (fail fast)? We can expose a query flag.

Alice Chen: Good idea. We'll make fallback behavior configurable per-route for the POC: ?fallback=graceful|strict and document the UX tradeoffs. Need to confirm pricing/charge behavior though — Acme commercial wants to know if fallback to cheaper model changes invoicing.

Devon Park: Billing note: tokens are billed based on the model that actually served the request. So if a request falls back to model-compact-v1, that usage will be charged at compact rates. We'll attach an appendix to the SOW that describes billing for fallbacks, plus an event log indicating when fallback happened.

Marisol Vega: Also confirm data residency: fallback stays in the same region/cluster and does not route to a different tenant or region. I'll add a line in the security questionnaire response: "Model-variant fallbacks execute in-customer cluster and share the same KMS and audit logs."

Ravi Patel: Action items for internal decision log and client-facing notes: 1) Devon run evals for compact vs standard and post numbers (ETA EOD today). 2) Jordan propose safe enqueue threshold + autoscale tweak and timeline (ETA tomorrow AM). 3) Product to document route-level fallback flag and default behavior (graceful). 4) Sales/legal: update SOW billing appendix and security Q response.

Devon Park: Ack — eval run queued, will post scores to this thread. Quick sample of what I'll measure: accuracy on 50 eval prompts, hallucination count, prompt-by-prompt delta.

Jordan Li: I'll test autoscaler tweak on a staging replica and post results. I think bumping desired by +2 idle buffer and lowering scale-up cooldown to 15s should fix the 11:23 pattern.

Alice Chen: Ellen — does that plan look acceptable to your team for POC sign-off cadence? If yes we'll update the POC timeline: 2 days for eval + 1 day autoscale changes + doc updates, then another controlled load run.

Ellen Rivera: Sounds reasonable. Please include the fallback header (X-Redwood-Fallback) in responses for our metrics. Also include a human-readable event in the logs so our SRE can alert on fallback rate > 5% per minute.

Marisol Vega: I'll draft the security questionnaire snippet and include KMS access pattern + confirmation that fallback does not leak keys or cross-tenant.

Alice Chen: Great. I'll create a short decision log entry and ping legal for the SOW appendix. Marking this thread for follow-up tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Reminder — set a follow-up reminder: in 24 hours to check eval numbers and autoscale test results.

Devon Park: Posting quick eval summary (prelim): model-standard-v2 hallucination=1.2%, latency 95th=210ms; model-compact-v1 hallucination=2.8%, latency 95th=180ms. Full matrix uploaded to GDrive: https://redwood.gdrive/ACME/poc-evals

Ravi Patel: Thanks Devon. Compact exceeds our <=2% hallucination threshold. For POC acceptance we should require <2% unless the client explicitly allows higher. Ellen, can you confirm if Acme will accept 3% for the fallback path only (i.e., as an allowed degradation under graceful mode)?

Ellen Rivera: We can't accept >2% for the primary path. For fallback/graceful we can tolerate up to 3% as long as it's clearly labeled and our UX shows a downgraded badge. We'll sign off on that with the above caveats.

Alice Chen: Noted. I'll update the acceptance criteria and SOW appendix accordingly. Closing the loop here — will post the formal decision-log doc once the autoscale test result is in. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
